page: Amazon Web Services r7a.xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9R14 processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, yielding a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it operates on the Nitro hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression and text processing also demonstrate strong performance. However, memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks is weak, falling into the bottom 25% at 37.49 GB/sec, while small-block cached read bandwidth and large-block write bandwidth remain average. Multi-core CPU execution, software compilation, and database operations perform within the average range. Large-model LLM inference is weak, though small-model text generation achieves average throughput.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r7a.xlarge offers a high-density DDR5 memory profile relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require extensive local storage or high-speed network baselines. It is well-suited for workloads such as in-memory databases, caching layers like Redis, text processing pipelines, and general-purpose database operations.
